posture.name: Audit log sealed
posture.detail: Yes: every entry carries seq, prev_hash and hash.

posture.name: Seal uses a secret key
posture.detail: HMAC-SHA256: only a holder of the key can write a chain that verifies.

posture.name: Seal chain verified
posture.detail: agentguard audit verify checked 14 sealed entries (seq 1 to 14): the chain is intact.

posture.name: Unreadable lines
posture.detail: Every line of the log files is an audit entry.

posture.name: Secrets masked in the log
posture.detail: Entries holding text that looks like a secret (an API key, token or password): 1. Is the server running with --audit-redact=false?

posture.name: Audit API requires an API key
posture.detail: Not checked: the report read the log files, not a server.

controls.title: Logical access to protected assets is restricted
controls.shows: Agent actions that reached AgentGuard were checked against a policy (the policy file's SHA-256 abababababab…): 12 decisions, 3 denied, broken down by scope and agent.

controls.title: Access from outside the system boundary is controlled
controls.shows: Actions reaching outside the agent (network, browser, MCP tools, LLM tool calls) went through AgentGuard; the scope and transport breakdowns and the deny rules show what was let through and what was blocked (2 scopes, 3 transports).

controls.title: System components are monitored for anomalies
controls.shows: Every decision is recorded in the audit log; its seal status is "intact", and the posture checks cover unreadable lines and unmasked secrets.

controls.title: Security events are evaluated
controls.shows: Entries sending an action to a person for approval: 4 (3 approval ids). On record as approved by a person: 1; denied by a person: 1. The top deny rules show which risky actions were stopped.

controls.title: Changes are authorized
controls.shows: The report names the policy file's SHA-256 abababababab…, so a reviewer can match it to an approved change. Actions the policy sends for approval (deploys, writes) needed a person's yes: see Approvals.

limits: The report counts what the audit log recorded. An action that never reached AgentGuard is not in it.
Approval outcomes show only when the agent came back with the approval id after a person decided. The log does not record the decision itself, who made it, or a request that timed out.
The policy SHA-256 is of the file as it was when the report was made. The audit log does not record which version of the policy made each decision.
The secret check uses the built-in patterns only, not a policy's notifications.redaction.extra_patterns.
Archives that no file links to, and archives already pruned by --audit-max-backups or --audit-max-age-days, are not read.
Entries a running server still holds in its buffer or its overflow file (<audit-log>.overflow.jsonl) are not in the log yet, so they are not counted.
